item.title: [infoq] 一份数据，多种用途：Spotify 用 RAP 打通分析与在线服务
item.description: Spotify has introduced Random Access Parquet (RAP), a storage architecture that adds an external index to Apache Parquet files so key-based point queries can run directly on a data lake without copying data to an operational store. The same dataset can then serve analytics, machine learning, AI agents, and low-latency online features. RAP works with Iceberg tables and includes layout optimizations like sorting and covering indexes to cut query overhead.

item.title: [hackernews] Tracking down the 16-year-old WAL-reset SQLite bug
item.description: Tailscale and SQLite developers traced repeated, hard-to-explain corruption incidents to a 16-year-old WAL-Reset data race in SQLite, then found a second bug involving stale expression indexes. It is a useful case study for anyone debugging concurrency or maintaining SQLite-backed systems.

item.title: [infoq] Dropbox 集成 MCP 与 Dash，将安全设计与代码审查连接起来
item.description: Dropbox is integrating its internal knowledge system Dash with code review via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), so security design artifacts surface directly in pull requests. After a PR is created, the system retrieves relevant threat models and security requirements from Dash and shows them in the review UI, cutting manual searches. It builds on Dash's permission-based retrieval, encryption, and audit logs, and the pattern can extend to compliance and governance workflows.

item.description: Instacart has launched Blueberry, an AI-assisted incident response system for on-call engineers. It spins up around 10 sub-agents, grounds them in over 14 years of incident history and internal ops data, then posts evidence-backed root-cause hypotheses directly in Slack, typically within about three minutes; diagnosis accuracy reportedly rose from 60% to above 90%. Blueberry gathers context and proposes fixes but does not make changes to production on its own.
